episode.title: How Abu Simbel Moved Mountains In 1968!

synopsis: Between 1964 and 1968, engineers meticulously dismantled and relocated the ancient Abu Simbel temples to save them from a rising lake.
narration: From 1964 to 1968, engineers faced an impossible task. They carefully cut the massive 13th-century-BC Abu Simbel temples into thousands of blocks, moving and meticulously rebuilding them, saving them from the rising waters of a new lake.

shots.prompt: A wide, sweeping shot showing the gigantic facade of the Great Temple of Ramesses II at Abu Simbel, partially submerged by rising, clear blue lake water. Small, 1960s-era work boats navigate near the base, dwarfed by the ancient monument, hinting at the impending challenge. The scale is immense.

A dramatic close-up on engineers in hard hats and period clothing, meticulously using modern cutting tools to saw through a colossal stone block, revealing the ancient hieroglyphs beneath the cut. Dust motes dance in the harsh desert light, emphasizing the precision and difficulty of the work.

music: A powerful, grand, and slightly mysterious orchestral piece, infused with rhythmic percussion and deep brass, evoking the monumental scale of ancient structures and modern engineering. The music should convey a sense of awe and relentless effort, building with a steady, driving pulse that underlines the colossal undertaking, concluding with an open, unresolved chord.
